newsitem.title: UK: EIB sets first sterling bond with euro clause.
newsitem.headline: EIB sets first sterling bond with euro clause.

text.p: The European Investment Bank on Thursday issued the first sterling debt offering with a clause allowing for its redenomination into euros should Britain adopt the single European Union currency, the arranging bank said.
BZW, the investment banking arm of Barclays Bank, lead managed the 500 million sterling ($810 million) bond which will be repaid in sterling/euros in December 2007.

Eurobonds with redenomination clauses will prove more liquid than those without such language, primary market players said, while deals which cannot be redenominated at the same time as underlying government bonds may quickly become illiquid.

However, as sterling is not among the currencies expected to adopt the euro at the first opportunity, in January 1999, the redenomination clause may just be an academic exercise in its case, analysts said.

For core EMU currencies, like the French franc, guilder and mark, retail and wholesale markets will use a mix of euros and the underlying currency from 1999 until July 2002, by which stage all financial instruments, including banknotes and coins, will have been replaced.
By the time sterling and other non-core European currencies join European economic and monetary union, probably early in the next millennium if at all, redenomination may be automatic, analysts said.
The first Eurobonds with euro redenomination clauses -- euro Eurobonds -- were only seen this year. They have been launched in several European currencies since, including the Ecu.
The EIB, which unreservedly sees EMU going ahead on January 1, 1999, has been to the fore in this new market.
It sees its role as both a borrower and lender expanding after EMU and wants investors to know there can be no questioning the liquidity of its paper.
The question of sterling's replacement by the euro has been a vexed issue during the ongoing election campaign in Britain.
Prime Minister John Major has had a testing time trying to keep rank and file Conservative Party members in line with his "wait and see" policy on EMU.
The opposition Labour Party, a very clear leader in opinion polls, also has an open view on the euro.
Euro Eurobonds will be traded in their underlying currency until EMU. Most will be fungible with other issues the borrower might launch in the future, creating jumbo euro Eurobonds.

J.P. Morgan, which lead managed the first euro deal, for Austria in francs, said at the time euro bonds will be super liquid because of their size and because of the pan-European trading aspect after EMU.
The EIB's sterling issue was priced to yield 0.12 percentage point over British government bonds. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7658 ($ = 0.615 British Pounds Sterling)
